entries.title: Why this, and not HTML→PDF?
entries.text: Most "HTML to PDF" tools drive a headless browser and screenshot the page — the result is an image, text is not selectable, and pagination is an afterthought. pdf-report-engine lays out, line-breaks, paginates and embeds glyphs in-process , emitting true vector text. It is built…

entries.title: Features
entries.text: Vector, selectable text Fonts embed as /Type0 → /CIDFontType2 composites with a /ToUnicode CMap, so text extracts cleanly — including CJK. Band pagination Jasper-style bands: title , pageHeader , detail , groupHeader/Footer , pageFooter , summary , plus a translucent background b…

entries.title: How it works
entries.text: Two entry points funnel through one pipeline: renderToBuffer(report, options?) — one-shot: IR in, PDF bytes out. createReport(report, options?) — the live pdfkit doc plus the paginated pages model, so you can stream yourself.

entries.title: 60-second taste
entries.text: Continue to Getting started for fonts, data-driven tables and the CLI.

entries.title: Requirements
entries.text: Node.js ≥ 18 — the package is ESM-only ( "type": "module" ). Runtime dependencies: pdfkit and fontkit . Everything else is a dev dependency.

entries.title: Install
entries.text: Pin a tag, branch or commit with a # suffix: Building from source: After npm run build , the package's exports map points at dist/ , so you can import { renderToBuffer } from 'pdf-report-engine' from any ESM project.

entries.title: Your first report (IR)
entries.text: The report is a plain data object — ReportDoc . It is serialisable, diffable and validatable without any parser. Without embedding fonts, the standard PDF base-14 fonts (like Helvetica ) render out of the box, so a first report needs nothing installed.

entries.title: Embedding fonts
entries.text: To use real font programs (and non-Latin scripts), register them with readFontFiles . It reads from disk paths or from bytes you already have. Prefer a graceful fallback: filter candidates with fs.existsSync() and pass fonts: [] when none are found — the base-14 fonts still rende…

entries.title: Running in the browser
entries.text: The core engine is pure JavaScript and bundles for the browser — the library graph has no top-level node:* imports . Two constraints remain: pdfkit itself needs Buffer /streams, so build with a Node-polyfill plugin (Vite: vite-plugin-node-polyfills ; webpack: resolve.fallback );…

entries.title: Web fonts & Google Fonts
entries.text: You don't have to fetch bytes by hand. When the HTML references a web font, the engine resolves and embeds it during renderToBuffer — the same code runs in Node and in the browser . htmlToReportDoc collects Google Fonts <link> / @import and inline @font-face rules into report.fon…

entries.text: Feed an array into dataSource ; the detail template expands once per row, groups produce breaks and subtotal footers, and column headers repeat on every page the table spans (set repeatHeader: false to opt out). Cells are not limited to text. Add blocks to a cell to stack any flo…

entries.title: Breaks & keep-together
entries.text: Pagination fills a vertical cursor down the page, one fragment at a time. A paragraph becomes one fragment per typeset line — that is why prose flows freely across pages — while a table row, an image, a chart, a barcode and a table-of-contents row are each a single fragment and t…

entries.title: Charts
entries.text: A chart block draws bar , line , area , pie , donut , combo , waterfall , scatter , bubble , radar , gauge and heatmap charts with the same primitives as the rest of the engine: real vector marks and selectable labels, no canvas and no charting library. A chart is laid out as one…

entries.title: Bookmarks, table of contents & links
entries.text: Every heading emits an outline entry — the bookmark tree PDF readers show in their sidebar. Entries nest by heading level automatically, and a heading on a later page still attaches under the chapter opened earlier. Any block with an id also becomes a named destination. A toc blo…

entries.title: QR codes & barcodes
entries.text: barcode blocks encode QR , Code 128 and EAN-13 as vector rectangles — no image is embedded, so codes stay crisp at any zoom. value is ordinary Content , so it can be a literal or a data binding. Field / attribute Meaning symbology / data-barcode qr , code128 or ean13 . value / da…

entries.title: Author with HTML
entries.text: Prefer markup? The adapter parses a forgiving HTML/CSS subset into the same IR. The HTML subset understands colspan / rowspan , per-cell colours and borders, data-band for page headers/footers, and running {PAGE} tokens. A block-level becomes an embedded image. You can set…

entries.title: Images (offline & online)
entries.text: An ImageBlock takes a local path, a data: URI, raw bytes, or an http(s) URL. Offline sources render synchronously; remote URLs are fetched by renderToBuffer 's pre-pass.

entries.title: SVG vector images
entries.text: An svg block draws an SVG document as real PDF paths — no rasterisation, no canvas, no resolution ceiling. Inline <svg> markup, data:image/svg+xml URIs, .svg file paths, raw bytes and remote http(s) URLs all take the same code path; the image pre-pass fetches remote sources befor…

entries.text: A display: flex container lays out any flow blocks along a row or a column. The engine implements a pragmatic CSS-flexbox subset: main-axis direction, optional wrap, justify-content , align-items / align-self , gap and per-item flex-grow / flex-shrink / flex-basis . A flex contai…

entries.title: Streaming with createReport
entries.text: The lower-level, synchronous entry returns the pdfkit doc and the paginated pages array, so you can pipe the bytes to any writable stream.

entries.title: Online images via a custom loader
entries.text: Point src at an http(s) URL and either let the built-in fetch run, or inject a resolveImage hook (proxy / auth / cache / test fixtures).

entries.title: Merged cells ( colSpan / rowSpan )
entries.text: Horizontal and vertical merges work in both the IR and the HTML subset. Author them on cells; the engine lays the run out as a single grid fragment so borders and fills line up. In HTML it is just the familiar attributes:

entries.title: Diagonal corner header (two-way table)
entries.text: A cross-tabulation table names both axes in one corner cell: a diagonal slash splits it into two triangles, the column-axis label above and the row-axis label below. Give a cell diagonal (IR) or data-diagonal (HTML). The row grows to fit both labels, and each label wraps toward i…

entries.title: Rich table cells
entries.text: A cell can hold any flow block, not just text. Give it blocks and the table lays the stack out inside the padded cell box — images, QR/barcodes, charts, nested tables and paragraphs all work. The row grows to the tallest cell and stays atomic for pagination, so a row never splits…

entries.text: Three primitives cover most conditional output: visible drops a block, row or cell; styleWhen applies a style while an expression is true; and colorScale paints a cell background by interpolating its number between two colours (each cell gets one flat fill, and dark fills switch…

entries.title: Page bands & running tokens (IR)
entries.text: Bands repeat on every page; {PAGE} / {TOTAL} (or $page.number / $page.total in expressions) resolve per page only inside bands.

entries.title: Page bands in HTML ( data-band )
entries.text: The same bands authored in markup: tag any block-level element with data-band="…" and the adapter lifts it out of the body flow into a repeated page band. Supported types: title , pageHeader , pageFooter , summary , background . An height on the element fixes the band height; run…
